# Hints

## General

- [The Python Tutorial***REMOVED***[the python tutorial***REMOVED*** can be a great introduction.
- [PEP 8***REMOVED***[pep8***REMOVED*** is the Python code style guide.
- [PEP 257***REMOVED***[PEP257***REMOVED*** details Python docstring conventions.
- [Numbers***REMOVED***[numbers***REMOVED*** in Python can be integers, floats, or complex.


## 1. Define expected bake time in minutes

- You need to [name***REMOVED***[naming***REMOVED*** a [constant***REMOVED***[constants***REMOVED***, and [assign***REMOVED***[assignment***REMOVED*** it an [integer***REMOVED***[numbers***REMOVED*** value.
  This constant should be the first thing after the docstring that is at the top of the file.
  Remember to remove the #TODO comment after defining the constant.

## 2. Calculate remaining bake time in minutes

- You need to define a [function***REMOVED***[defining functions***REMOVED*** with a single parameter representing the time elapsed so far.
- Use the [mathematical operator for subtraction***REMOVED***[numbers***REMOVED*** to subtract values.
- This function should [return a value***REMOVED***[return***REMOVED***.

## 3. Calculate preparation time in minutes

- You need to define a [function***REMOVED***[defining functions***REMOVED*** with a single parameter representing the number of layers.
- Use the [mathematical operator for multiplication***REMOVED***[numbers***REMOVED*** to multiply values.
- You can define a PREPARATION_TIME _constant_ for the time in minutes per layer rather than using a ["magic
  number"***REMOVED***[magic-numbers***REMOVED*** in your code.
- This function should [return a value***REMOVED***[return***REMOVED***.

## 4. Calculate total elapsed cooking time (prep + bake) in minutes

- You need to define a [function***REMOVED***[defining functions***REMOVED*** with two parameters.
- Remember: you can always _call_ a function you've defined previously.
- You can use the [mathematical operator for addition***REMOVED***[python as a calculator***REMOVED*** to sum values.
- This function should [return a value***REMOVED***[return***REMOVED***.

## 5. Update the recipe with notes

- Clearly [commenting***REMOVED***[comments***REMOVED*** and [documenting***REMOVED***[docstrings***REMOVED*** your code according to [PEP257***REMOVED***[pep257***REMOVED*** is always recommended.
- Some examples of Google-style docstrings can be found in the Sphinx documentation for the [napoleon module***REMOVED***[napoleon***REMOVED***.
